artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Craig Sheppard complained that Highlands Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures after finding a strong presumption of guilt, and by failing to institute process within one year as required by BCO 32-20. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that BCO 31-2 mandates process upon finding a strong presumption of guilt, and that Presbytery was debarred from prosecution because the alleged offense occurred in 2017 and timely process was never instituted; three members dissented on the BCO 32-20 issue, arguing it was not a true statute of limitations and that the matter was never a 'case of scandal.'

artifacts.synopsis: TE Ryan Speck complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Greg Johnson regarding four allegations arising from his involvement in and teaching at the Revoice 2018 conference; the SJC sustained the complaint in part on Issue 1 (particularly regarding Theological Judgments 2, 3, and 5 about terminology, gay identity, and spiritual friendship), denied Issues 2 and 3, and remanded the matter to Missouri Presbytery for a new hearing on specific questions.

artifacts.title: Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

artifacts.title: Marusich v. Central Indiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC remanded the case to Central Indiana Presbytery with instructions to appoint a committee to reinvestigate under BCO 31-2, after its non-judicial commission declined to find a strong presumption of guilt against an accused teaching elder. The dissent argued the SJC failed to give proper great deference under BCO 39-3.3 to the presbytery's investigative commission's discretionary judgment declining to indict, and that the BCO does not require the investigative procedures ordered by the Decision.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Sartorius complained that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in acquitting TE Greg Lawrence on five charges of holding Federal Vision and non-confessional views on baptism, perseverance, and covenant of works at a second trial (2015); the SJC denied the complaint 22-1, holding that the complainant failed to demonstrate clear error in the trial court's factual finding and that BCO 39-3.2 requires great deference to the lower court's verdict. A concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively discussed standards of appellate review, defendant testimony supporting the acquittal, and raised concerns about due process rights of acquitted persons.

artifacts.title: Fordice v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Fordice complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery erred by allowing TE Nathan Lewis to confess under BCO 38-1 and closing the matter without adequate process, after its own investigative committee had found a strong presumption of guilt on 18 allegations. The SJC unanimously sustained the complaint and remanded the case to PNW, finding that while use of BCO 38-1 was not itself error, the approved statement of facts was not 'full' as required because it failed to correlate with the underlying allegations.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.

artifacts.synopsis: McNeil complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in denying his complaint against the Session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after the Session had already censured him for abusive behavior; the SJC denied the complaint, applying a standard of great deference to the lower court and finding no clear procedural error.

artifacts.title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

TE James Urish complained that Presbytery erred in sustaining the candidate's exam. The SJC affirmed Presbytery's decision, finding no clear error, as neither the Westminster Standards nor the BCO explicitly address this specific application of 1 Timothy 2:12.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission heard an appeal by TE John Grady from his conviction and censure by Southwest Florida Presbytery. The Commission sustained three of seven error specifications but found only one materially prejudicial. Critically, the Commission found that Presbytery misapplied BCO 13-9.c by claiming power to direct the minister to resign and then censuring him for refusal to comply; the Commission vacated the censure and remanded for reconsideration of appropriate punishment while the administrative suspension under BCO 31-10 remained in effect.

The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.

artifacts.synopsis: Westminster Presbytery was found to have erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation of secret taping by TE Frank Smith by failing to obtain full witness testimony and investigate legal ramifications; case remanded. The court found no proof of partiality and declined to require establishment of unbiblical criteria for secret taping. Vote: 18 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE Frederick Neikirk), 2 recused, 1 abstained, 2 absent.

artifacts.title: Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Merriam appealed his conviction by Tennessee Valley Presbytery on charges of violating ordination vows, including being contumacious toward brethren, failing to maintain church peace, and lacking exemplary piety. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error by the lower court and affirming TVP's procedures and judgment.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.

artifacts.synopsis: St. Paul Session and others complained that Central Florida Presbytery erred in sustaining the report of a commission that investigated but did not bring to trial charges against TE John Hutchinson, and also regarding a related complaint against the Session of Christ Church, Jacksonville. The SJC denied the complaint, finding CFP acted within its right to determine investigation procedures under BCO 31-2, with a dissent arguing CFP failed to investigate the substance of the 45 specific charges.
